cells.tense: You are holding the whole pattern in view and still standing inside it.
cells.ask: Before you finish today's list, say what you just worked out, in one sentence, to the person who would miss it most.
cells.core:
You can read the shape of a situation without stepping out of it. People come to you to hear what's actually going on, because when you say it they feel it land. The picture stays whole while you're in it.

What's available now is the pull of other people — not to solve them, just to feel alongside them. The read you're making of someone close is sharp enough. Let some of it come out as care instead of commentary, and the recognition holds you both instead of flattening one. Keeping this costs you the temptation to name everything you notice; not every piece needs saying.

cells.tense: You will have the whole pattern mapped before anyone has finished telling you the situation.
cells.ask: Ask one question about the situation and wait through the answer without reaching for a structure to fit it into.
cells.core:
A pattern seen well just shows itself and opens something instead of closing it. You take in what's true across the whole thing, put words to it without forcing them, and let the pieces keep their room to move.

Right now you're ahead of it. The shape gets seen before the facts settle, so you start steering — moving pieces before they've arrived, giving orders to something still forming. The clarity is real; the timing isn't yours yet. There is nothing to organise in a thing that hasn't happened. Say less than you can see, and let the situation finish being itself before you name it.

cells.tense: You saw something whole once, and you have been standing at that door since.
cells.ask: Say one thing you know out loud to someone who is trying to learn the same thing, without needing them to agree.
cells.core:
The picture won't come together now. You used to pull the whole shape into one piece in a moment — not to judge, just to see — and these days the parts arrive one at a time and won't hold still. It isn't that the skill left. You just haven't looked from the outside in a while.

What's missing is the shared meaning underneath it: what the reading is for. Understanding that exists only inside your own head stops being understanding and starts being a room you're alone in. Put one real thing out to another person — one insight passed along simply because it's true — and the whole shape starts holding again.
cells.sheetLine: Seeing lost its meaning, and meaning brings it back.
cells.verb: seeing the shape the whole thing makes
cells.place: the outside view from inside the room

cells.tense: You are reading the whole pattern in this room and talking as if it were the weather.
cells.ask: Name one pattern you've spotted out loud and say it belongs to you to see, not to the situation.
cells.core:
Said plainly, the read lands as a gift: knowing where a group is heading, putting it into words one time, and watching the room come clear. The read was yours to offer the whole while.

Right now you track how it all fits — what a group is doing, where a plan is going, what someone means under their words — and you've never once said so. It shows up as being cancelled, or not arguing, or vaguely agreeing with a version that isn't yours. The claim on the read is what's missing, not the skill. Say that one piece in plain words and stay there while the room adjusts. Your eye has been open the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: You're already reading the room. Admit it out loud.
